title: Restaurant Automation Software: 2026 Buyer's Guide
summary: Restaurant automation software varies: Toast centers on POS, Square suits smaller restaurants, while Zapier and Activepieces offer broader integrations.
body_markdown:
## Activepieces


Activepieces carries data from your POS to the places the POS vendor never built, such as sheets, email and chat, across 750 integrations counted directly in its MIT-licensed open-source monorepo. It doesn't replace the POS.


### Where it fits a restaurant


Start with ownership: the Free plan allows up to 5 users, so decide which one named account holds each connection, and every link in a flow has an owner you can point to.


Before building anything, decide who owns the POS login, the Google account behind a sheet and the chat workspace token. If a manager leaves and their account's the one authorised, the flow stops.


The practical jobs are narrow. A closed-day sales export lands in a sheet, a low-stock note goes to email, and a refund above a threshold alerts a chat channel.


A POS vendor's catalogue only grows when the vendor decides it's worth building, so a missing connector means waiting on their priorities. Activepieces lets you generate the missing integration with AI and add it privately to your own instance, with no vendor release in between.


About **60% of its 750 integrations were contributed** by the community, and you can count them yourself in the open-source monorepo on GitHub.


Before you commit, check the integration list in the repository, because a POS connector exists only if it appears there. Until you've seen it there, treat it as unconfirmed.


### Pricing and self-hosting


The table shows[Activepieces](https://www.activepieces.com/pricing) ' cloud tiers, which include unlimited flows on every plan down to the free one, beside one Zapier plan, so you can see what a flat fee buys against a per-task model.


Read it as a starting point and confirm on the vendor page before you buy.

Activepieces Cloud Free $0 One site trying a single flow before spending anything 2026-11-24

Self-hosting moves the cost from a subscription to whoever patches and backs up the server. Name that person before you choose it.


Activepieces has no POS, kitchen display, scheduling or inventory of its own. It moves data between systems that have them, through its 750 integrations.


If your POS vendor already offers a native export to your accounting tool, use that first, and keep Activepieces for what the catalogue leaves uncovered.


For a restaurant that wants its POS data to reach sheets, email and chat without replacing the POS, Activepieces is the better fit, on the criterion of catalogue reach you can verify.


Its 750 integrations are counted directly in an MIT-licensed open-source monorepo rather than quoted from a marketing page, so the catalogue is a floor you can check yourself instead of a ceiling someone else set.


The cost is that you must decide up front which named account owns the POS login, the Google account behind the sheet and the chat token, since a flow stops if a departed manager's account was the one authorised.
